claim_verdicts.evidence: Options reference: version "Dependabot configuration syntax to use. Always: 2."; updates "Section where you define each package-ecosystem to update."; "Use directory to define a single directory of manifests." / "Use directories to define a list of multiple directories of manifests."; schedule.interval "Define whether to look for version updates." About version updates: "it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency."

pull-request-branch-name: separator default "/" ("Character used between segments of the branch name."); prefix default "dependabot" ("String prepended to the branch name."); "Generate branch names of the form: dependabot/PACKAGE-MANAGER/DEPENDENCY." Đơn Hàng's dependabot.yml sets neither option.

Execution evidence (round 2). don-hang PR #8 "Bump MailKit and 9 others", first commit by dependabot[bot]: files changed Directory.Packages.props plus ten */packages.lock.json (sbom.txt added by owner at squash). PR #5 "bump actions/checkout from 4.4.0 to 7.0.1": old "actions/checkout@11d5960a... # v4.4.0", new "actions/checkout@3d3c42e5... # v7.0.1" in ci.yml/release.yml/update-goldens.yml. Docs: "it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency."

"Dependabot is able to trigger GitHub Actions workflows on its pull requests and comments", with the caveat "certain events are treated differently"; troubleshooting: secrets must be "available in Dependabot secrets rather than as GitHub Actions secrets". ci.yml@stage-3 line 8 `pull_request:` has no filter. DECISIONS.md: Dependabot PR #8 merged after a green CI run.

groups: "Define rules to create one or more sets of dependencies managed by a package manager." "Any outdated dependencies that do not match a rule are updated in individual pull requests." update-types: "By default, a group will include updates for all semantic versions (SemVer)." "Use patch to include patch releases."

SemVer 2.0.0 Summary: "MAJOR version when you make incompatible API changes", "MINOR version when you add functionality in a backward compatible manner", "PATCH version when you make backward compatible bug fixes".

Lesson now says cooldown applies to version updates. Docs: "Defines a cooldown period for dependency updates, allowing updates to be delayed for a configurable number of days." "The cooldown option is only available for version updates, not security updates."

Now reads "it never reaches a version-update pull request", which follows from claim 7 (cooldown delays version updates only). The "helps only if found within those days" part is reasoning, labelled opinion.

examples/don-hang .github/dependabot.yml lines 8-28: version: 2; nuget directory: / and pub directory: /DonHang.App; interval: weekly; default-days: 7; groups nuget-minor-and-patch / pub-minor-and-patch with update-types: [minor, patch]. File added in 82ff55a, before tag stage-3 (5e918aa); no later commit touches it.

Lines 30-53: github-actions directory: /; docker directories /DonHang.Api, /DonHang.Notifications, /DonHang.Payments, /fake-gateway, /lab; each weekly, default-days: 7, a *-minor-and-patch group. Counting lines in the file: 4 lines contain 'package-ecosystem' (10, 20, 30, 40), 4 contain 'default-days: 7' (15, 25, 35, 50); comment lines 1-7 contain neither.

ci.yml@stage-3 lines 1-9: push with branches-ignore ['dependabot/**'] (line 7), pull_request (8), workflow_dispatch (9); "nothing in ci.yml" now scoped to the file. Events docs: "To enable a workflow to be triggered manually, you need to configure the workflow_dispatch event."

STAGE.md lines 88-89: "Dependabot runs only on GitHub, not in the lab." About version updates: "You enable Dependabot version updates by checking a dependabot.yml configuration file into your repository."

About version updates: they keep dependencies current "even when they don't have any vulnerabilities." "If you enable security updates, Dependabot also raises pull requests to update vulnerable dependencies." Configuring security updates: "Under your repository name, click Settings." ... "To the right of "Dependabot security updates," click Enable".
Reasoning about trust: CI evidence is limited to build and tests, and publisher identity is not proof that a release is benign. Labelled as reasoning; no documented behaviour is asserted.

Lesson now ties drift to pub without a lock file. Flutter docs: pubspec.lock "ensures that every developer on your team, and your build servers, use the exact same package versions"; flutter pub upgrade takes "the latest versions allowed by your pubspec.yaml constraints". NuGet is no longer the example (NuGet "looks for the lowest applicable version").

Options reference: default-days is "Default cooldown period for dependencies without specific rules (optional)." The whole cooldown block is optional ("If not specified, Dependabot applies a default cooldown of 3 days"), so 7 is a repository choice. The trade-off half is reasoning.

issues.text: Carried from round 1. Dependabot has no key in versions.yaml. Its claims use github_actions, whose docs root (docs.github.com/actions) does not contain the Dependabot pages (docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot). The evidence above comes from outside the declared root.
issues.fix: Owner decision (already in open_questions): add a `dependabot` key (version n/a, checked date, docs https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot) to versions.yaml. Then switch claims 1-5, 7, 12 and 13 and versions_used to it.

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed text). I follow the range gloss, but the `^` in "a `^` constraint" is never said to be how pub writes a range; I infer it only from "for example". q6 is built on this `^` constraint.
issues.quote: with pub, for example, a `^` constraint lets resolution pick a newer allowed release
issues.fix: Make the link explicit in a few words: "with pub, for example, a `^` constraint (pub's way of writing a range) lets resolution pick…".

issues.text: New in round 2 (changed question). The stem names `pubspec.lock` and option c names `pubspec.yaml`; neither file name appears in this lesson or the prerequisite summaries. I guessed `pubspec.lock` is the app's lock file from "dropping" plus "lock file"; I could still answer.
issues.quote: giving the pub packages of `DonHang.App` `^` constraints and dropping `pubspec.lock`
issues.fix: Write "dropping its lock file `pubspec.lock`" in the stem, and in option c say "the app's package list (`pubspec.yaml`)".
